market_summary: 129 listings match the filters this week, with no new arrivals, one listing gone (Nädhult 2:14 in Hylte at 1 500 000 kr, gone after 22 days) and no price cuts. The median asking price is 2 995 000 kr and the median is 228 000 kr per ha. Småland carries the most supply with 42 listings, Göteborg hinterland is still the most expensive at a 3 550 000 kr median, and Dalsland/Värmland stays the cheapest. The only movement was Björkesbacka Bäckaskog in Mark, where bidding has pushed the price from 3 995 000 kr to 4 575 000 kr, which shows that close-in gårdar still draw competition while the wider market stays slow. For a buyer this week there is nothing new to view, so the standing list holds and negotiation room on the older listings remains.

entries.prepping_why: Water on or next to the land and some forest across 7.25 ha give a reasonable base, and at 0.8 hours from Göteborg it is the easiest kind of retreat to reach on one tank. The listing says nothing about a well, wood heating or seclusion, so the core survival must-haves are unconfirmed.
entries.invest_why: Bidding has already lifted the price to 4 575 000 kr, about 631 000 kr per ha, close to three times the 228 000 kr median, so you are paying for location rather than land value. Göteborg hinterland resells well, but at this level there is little room for the forest to carry the price and a winning bid would likely go higher still.
entries.rank_why: Proximity and a lake or stream lift it, but a bid-driven price near the 5 000 000 kr ceiling with no condition data holds it well below cheaper Småland and Halland gårdar in the same band.
entries.maintenance: Unknown: the listing gives no build year, facade, roof or window information, so the low-maintenance test cannot be passed on what is published.
entries.recommendation: Skip, because bidding has already pushed it about 580 000 kr over the asking price to the top of the budget, and nothing published shows that the house meets the low-maintenance spec.
